result_text:
The mock-folder rule now matches any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock`, and the new test and the existing `SourceFileFilterTest` pass (7 tests, 0 failures).

**Change**

- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393): the two folder rules now use `[^/]*` for the rest of the folder name instead of `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`:
  - `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`
  - `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`

  The old character class required at least one character after `mock`, so a bare `mock/` was missed. It also rejected punctuation and non-ASCII characters. `[^/]*` stays inside one path segment, so `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/` and files like `mock.java` or `mockery.java` still don't match. The existing `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` cases still match.
- `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/SourceFileFilterTest.java`: added `testMockFoldersAreTestCode`. It checks the new cases (plain `mock`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe`, `mock模拟`, a Windows-style path) and the negative cases (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`) against the test-file conventions.

Backslash paths work through the existing normalisation in `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches`. I didn't run a full analysis on the elasticsearch repo, so the 2,500-line figure is not re-verified. I also did not commit.
